Old saves: parties A, B, C become 1, 2, 3, keeping names, members and order; created and last-edited dates are set to the date of the change.

Emblems and backgrounds come from a shared list of Roblox asset IDs the user will upload; the save stores a short key. The list has a "default" entry: before art exists the emblem is drawn as a navy tile with a bronze border and the party number, and the background is the plain theme navy; when art arrives "default" points to the first emblem and background, so uncustomised parties update by themselves. A removed key falls back to "default"; keys are never reused. The background fills only the party header strip - no portrait background. Grid picker: tapping an option previews it at once, Done saves, Cancel reverts.

Member slot 1 is the leader. The leader is display only and changes nothing in battle. "Make leader" swaps that unit into slot 1. Filled portrait tap: View loadout / Make leader (not shown for slot 1) / Remove. Empty "+" tap: Add units picker (roster in the Loadout portrait style; units already in the party ticked; units on dispatch greyed and not tappable; pick several, then Done or Cancel). Units on dispatch can't be added; members who go on dispatch stay in the party, greyed with a dispatch icon, and are skipped at deployment. A unit can belong to more than one party (locked 2026-10-14). Units sold or lost leave every party automatically. "View loadout" opens INFO with that unit selected.

Saved parties: up to 5, numbered Party 1-5, created and deleted by the player, each with a name, motto, emblem and header background, managed on the Loadout PARTIES tab (loadout_ui_spec 102-116). Member slot 1 is the leader (display only). A saved party holds UP TO 7 units (7 = the maximum deployment ceiling, NOT a required or fixed count): a player with fewer units (e.g. 3) still forms a valid party and can go on quests, fielding what they have. The per-quest deployable cap (see Deployment) limits how many of the party actually deploy, resolved at the deployment phase. Units away on dispatch show greyed out and cannot be picked.

After a quest is ACCEPTED, the player enters a mostly-optional prep menu. OPTIONAL items: Manage Unit Loadout (existing loadout screen) and Edit Party Roster (opens the Loadout PARTIES tab). MANDATORY, ORDERED spine: Choose Party to deploy (opens the PARTIES tab in pick mode) -> Sortie. 'Sortie' is the final confirmation screen (it is the existing Depart briefing, id 11) showing the quest, the generated map, and battle details, with a go / back-out choice. Nothing in this menu is load-bearing for timing (asset availability is checked at server start, not here).
